summary: Using a Dexcom G7, ONE+ or Stelo with AAPS. Four ways are covered: xDrip connecting directly, BYODA, xDrip as a companion to the Dexcom app, and Juggluco. Most steps happen in xDrip, Android or Juggluco; in AAPS the reader selects the xDrip+ BG source.

sections.heading: Fundamental in advance
sections.summary: Notes that G7, ONE+ and Stelo values are not smoothed and points to the smoothing page.

sections.heading: 1. xDrip (direct connection to G7, ONE+ or Stelo)
sections.summary: Connecting xDrip directly to the sensor in place of the Dexcom app, then selecting xDrip+ as the BG source in AAPS.

sections.heading: 2. Build Your Own Dexcom App (G7 only)
sections.summary: Installing BYODA for the G7 in place of the official Dexcom app and entering the sensor code.

sections.heading: 3. xDrip Companion App (G7, ONE+ and Stelo)
sections.summary: Explains companion mode: the Dexcom app keeps the sensor and xDrip forwards its values to AAPS. AAPS does not treat this as a trusted BG source, so SMBs are restricted.

sections.heading: Read the Dexcom app notifications
sections.summary: Setting xDrip's hardware data source to Companion App and allowing it notification access in Android, including the restricted-settings workaround. All labels belong to xDrip or Android.

sections.heading: Companion Bluetooth (G7)
sections.summary: Turning on Companion Bluetooth in xDrip's Bluetooth settings so it reads the G7's readings directly, and forgetting old sensors in Android Bluetooth settings. xDrip and Android labels only.

sections.heading: Configuration in AAPS
sections.summary: Selecting xDrip+ as the BG source in AAPS for companion mode.

sections.heading: 4. Juggluco (G7 and ONE+)
sections.summary: Moving the sensor to Juggluco: stopping the previous app, forgetting the sensor in Android Bluetooth, and pairing in Juggluco by scanning the applicator. No AAPS labels.
